words.gloss: marma (vital point of the body); division

hindi: अब इसलिए हम मर्मविभाग शारीर की व्याख्या करेंगे, अर्थात् मर्म यानी शरीर के प्राणस्थानों के विभाजन की।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Śārīra (the section on the body) called Marmavibhāga, the division of the marmas (vital points of the body).
notes: marma is a doctrinal term and is kept with a short gloss, not forced into a modern equivalent. 'śārīram' is taken as the name of the section (as at the opening of other chapters of this part); it could also be read as an adjective 'bodily' agreeing with vibhāgam.

words.gloss: seven; more, additional (on a conjectural reading; printed sama-uttara)

hindi: एक सौ सात मर्म, अनुमानित पाठ पर, यानी सौ और सात अधिक।
english: A hundred and seven marmas (on a conjectural reading: a hundred with seven more).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sama-uttara' gives no usable sense; pta -> ma is a seen OCR confusion in this book; with 'saptottara' (a hundred with seven more) the total fits line 3 (card 3) (44 + 26 + 37 = 107)

notes: The reading 'saptottaram' is conjectural and is marked so in the translations; the count 107 rests on it and on the sum of line 3 (card 3). Nominal statement with no verb; none is supplied. GROUPING: appears to open the enumeration continued in 3.

words.gloss: seven; thirty (thirty-seven, on a conjectural reading)

hindi: उनमें शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में चवालीस, अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में छब्बीस, और ऊपर, अनुमानित पाठ पर, सैंतीस।
english: Among these: forty-four in the limbs (śākhā), twenty-six in the trunk (antarādhi), and above, thirty-seven (on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: 'samaṃtriśat' is not a numeral; pta -> ma is a seen OCR confusion, and the anusvara stands after ma instead of after tri (triṃśat); 44 + 26 + 37 = 107 matches the total of line 2 (card 2) (conjectured)

notes: The numbers 44 and 26 are printed and translated exactly. 'ūrdhvam' = above, i.e. the upper part of the body (the neck and head are the contents of the later units); this is not stated in the line. antarādhi = trunk is the standard sense. Nominal sentence, no verb supplied. GROUPING: appears to continue 2.

hindi: अब प्रत्येक सक्थि यानी पूरे निचले अंग में, मध्यमा अंगुली के समीप, पैर के तलवे के बीच तलहृदय नामक मर्म; वहाँ बिंधे हुए की पीड़ा से मृत्यु।
english: Now, in each sakthi (lower limb), near the middle toe, in the middle of the sole of the foot, the marma named talahṛdaya (sole-heart); for one pierced there, death through pain.
notes: 'sakthi' (thigh) is printed as a locative in -i (allowed for neuters in -i). Since the marma lies in the sole, sakthi here evidently stands for the whole lower limb; the translation keeps 'thigh'. 'abhitaḥ' with the accusative is taken as 'near, around'. 'madhyamāṅguli' = middle toe here. 'ekaikasmin' (m./n.) agrees with sakthi. Death 'through pain' is the text's wording; nothing is added. First unit of the limb marmas. Reviewer: translations now render sakthi as 'lower limb' (the sole marma cannot lie in the thigh); the earlier remark that the translation keeps 'thigh' is superseded.
lines_deva: अथैकैकस्मिन्सक्थि मध्यमांगुलिमभितो मध्ये पादतलस्य तलहृदयं नाम मर्म तत्र विद्धस्य रुजया मरणं
lines_iast: athaikaikasminsakthi madhyamāṃgulimabhito madhye pādatalasya talahṛdayaṃ nāma marma tatra viddhasya rujayā maraṇaṃ

hindi: अँगूठे और अंगुली के बीच क्षिप्र; वहाँ आक्षेपक यानी सम्भवतः ऐंठन के दौरे से मृत्यु।
english: Between the big toe (aṅguṣṭha) and the toe (aṅguli), kṣipra; there, death by ākṣepaka (probably a convulsive spasm).
notes: The printed 'aṅguṣṭhāṅgulyoḥ' is taken as 'of the big toe and the (next) toe'; the word aṅguli is general (finger or toe), and 'the next toe' is understood, not stated. That kṣipra is a marma is understood from the series (the next unit says 'above kṣipra'). ākṣepaka = convulsive spasm: probable. The print joins kṣipraṃ + tatra + ākṣepakeṇa; split without a flag.

words.gloss: foot; whirling; trembling (on a conjectural reading)

hindi: क्षिप्र के ऊपर दो अंगुल यानी दो उँगली-चौड़ाई पर, दोनों ओर, कूर्च; वहाँ, अनुमानित पाठ पर, पाँव का भ्रमण यानी घूमना और काँपना होते हैं।
english: Two aṅgulas (finger-breadths) above kṣipra, on both sides, kūrca; there, on a conjectural reading, whirling (bhramaṇa) and trembling (vepana) of the foot occur.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dvyaṅgulam ubhayataḥ' is the form of lines 23-24 (card 23/24); 'au' for 'amu' looks like a print slip
possible: 'ruya' is not a word; the dual verb bhavataḥ suits two items (bhramaṇa, vepana); 'ruya' may be a stray insertion, or a damaged rujā (pain), which would make three items

notes: Doubled -rcc- in 'kūrccaḥ' is normalised to kūrca (print habit, as in 7 and 36). The word 'pādaruyabhramaṇavepane' is damaged: the reading with 'ruya' dropped is a conjecture and is marked as such in both translations. Alternative if 'ruya' stands for rujā: pain, whirling and trembling of the foot. The plural form kūrcau (two kūrca) may be intended since 'ubhayataḥ' (both sides) is used; the singular is kept as printed.
lines_deva: क्षिप्रस्योपरि द्व्यंगुलउभयतः कूर्च्चः तत्र पादरुयभ्रमणवेपने भवतः
lines_iast: kṣiprasyopari dvyaṃgulaubhayataḥ kūrccaḥ tatra pādaruyabhramaṇavepane bhavataḥ

hindi: टखने के जोड़ के नीचे कूर्चशिर; वहाँ, अनुमानित पाठ पर, पीड़ा और सूजन।
english: Below the ankle-joint (gulpha-saṃdhi), kūrcaśiras (head of the kūrca); there, on a conjectural reading, pain (rujā) and swelling (śopha).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śoka' (grief) does not suit a bodily sign in a marma list; 'śopha' (swelling) is the usual companion of pain (compare śopha in line 11 (card 11)); ka/pha is a plausible misreading

notes: The correction śoka -> śopha is a conjecture, marked in both translations. gulpha = ankle (standard). Doubled -rcc- normalised (see 6). Nominal sentence.

hindi: पैर और जंघा यानी घुटने से नीचे की टाँग के जोड़ पर गुल्फ यानी टखना; वहाँ पीड़ा, सक्थि यानी जाँघ का अकड़ जाना, अथवा जड़ता यानी सुन्नपन।
english: At the joining of the foot and the shank (jaṅghā), the gulpha (ankle); there, pain, stiffness of the sakthi (thigh), or numbness (jaḍatā).
notes: The three signs are read as alternatives ('or' at the end). jaḍatā = numbness or torpor; 'numbness' is the plainer sense for a limb. jaṅghā = shank (calf/lower leg), not the Hindi 'thigh' sense. 'sakthi' as in 4 may mean the whole leg; kept as 'thigh'.
lines_deva: पादजंघयोः संधाने गुल्फः तत्र रुक् स्तब्धसक्थिता जडता वा
lines_iast: pādajaṃghayoḥ saṃdhāne gulphaḥ tatra ruk stabdhasakthitā jaḍatā vā

words.gloss: heel (pārṣṇi, on a conjectural reading; printed pāṇi, hand); beginning from

hindi: एड़ी से, अनुमानित पाठ पर, बारह अंगुल पर, जंघा यानी घुटने से नीचे की टाँग के बीच इन्द्रबस्ति; वहाँ शोणित यानी रक्त के क्षय से मृत्यु।
english: Starting from the heel (on a conjectural reading), at twelve aṅgulas, in the middle of the shank (jaṅghā), indrabasti; there, death from loss of blood (śoṇita).

text_flags.why: possible: 'pāṇi' (hand) cannot start a measurement along the leg; 'pārṣṇi' (heel) fits, and rṣṇ -> ṇ is a plausible slip
near certain: 'kṣyāt' lacks the a of kṣayāt; the n before m is the regular sandhi of t

notes: The heel reading is a conjecture and is marked in the translations. In indrabasti 'basti' is part of a marma name (bladder/bag); it is not the urinary organ of line 19 (card 19). Printed 'pāṇi' could in principle be kept as 'the hand' but that fails the sense.

hindi: जंघा यानी घुटने से नीचे की टाँग और ऊरु यानी जाँघ के जोड़ पर जानु यानी घुटना; वहाँ लंगड़ापन।
english: At the joining of the shank (jaṅghā) and the thigh (ūru), the jānu (knee); there, lameness (khañjatā).
notes: Nominal sentence; no verb supplied.

words.gloss: āṇi (marma name; literally a pin or linchpin)

hindi: जानु यानी घुटने से तीन अंगुल ऊपर, दोनों ओर, आणि; वहाँ सूजन की वृद्धि और सक्थि यानी जाँघ का अकड़ जाना।
english: Three aṅgulas above the knee (jānu), on both sides, āṇi; there, increase of swelling (śopha) and stiffness of the sakthi (thigh).
notes: The print joins ubhayataḥ and āṇiḥ (ubhayata + āṇiḥ, regular sandhi aḥ + ā giving the hiatus ubhayata āṇiḥ); split without a flag. āṇi is read as the marma name.

hindi: ऊरु यानी जाँघ के बीच उर्वी; वहाँ रक्त के क्षय से सक्थि यानी जाँघ का शोष यानी सूखकर क्षीण होना।
english: In the middle of the thigh (ūru), urvī; there, from loss of blood (rakta), wasting (śoṣa) of the sakthi (thigh).
notes: The print joins 'tatra' and 'raktakṣayāt' without a space (no sandhi); split without a flag. Nominal sentence.

words.gloss: pakṣāghāta (paralysis of one side, hemiplegia; standard)

hindi: और उर्वी के ऊपर तथा वंक्षण यानी जाँघ और पेड़ू के जोड़ के नीचे, ऊरु यानी जाँघ के मूल में, लोहित नामक; वहाँ रक्त के क्षय से पक्षाघात यानी एक ओर के अंगों का लकवा।
english: And above urvī and below the groin-joint (vaṅkṣaṇa-saṃdhi), at the root of the thigh, the one named lohita ('red'); there, from loss of blood (rakta), pakṣāghāta (hemiplegia, paralysis of one side).
notes: 'ūrvyāḥ tu' is read with 'ūrdhvam' (above urvī) and 'adhaḥ' with the groin-joint (below it). The noun 'marma' is understood with 'lohitākhyam' (neuter); lohita here is the marma name. pakṣāghāta = paralysis of one half of the body (hemiplegia): standard.

words.gloss: ṣāṇḍhya (impotence, the state of a ṣaṇḍha; probable)

hindi: वंक्षण यानी जाँघ और पेड़ू के जोड़ तथा वृषण यानी अण्डकोष के बीच विटप; वहाँ षाण्ढ्य यानी सम्भवतः नपुंसकता अथवा शुक्र यानी वीर्य की अल्पता।
english: Between the groin (vaṅkṣaṇa) and the testes (vṛṣaṇa), viṭapa; there, ṣāṇḍhya (impotence, probably) or scantiness of śukra (semen).

text_flags.why: near certain: 'śukṛtā' is not a word; alpa-śukra-tā (scantiness of semen) fits; ra -> ṛ is a print slip

notes: ṣāṇḍhya = state of a ṣaṇḍha (a man lacking virility): impotence is the probable modern sense. vṛṣaṇa = testes (it can also mean the scrotum).

hindi: सक्थि यानी निचले अंग के समान, दोनों भुजाओं में।
english: Like the sakthi (lower limb), in the two arms (bāhu).
notes: Elliptical: no verb and no marma named. The plain sense is that the arms have marmas corresponding to those of the sakthi, but the line does not say which; nothing is supplied. GROUPING: appears to be continued by 16 and 17, which give the differences for the arms.

hindi: परन्तु विशेष: गुल्फ—मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई, और वैसे ही जानु—कूर्पर यानी कोहनी; उन दोनों के बिंधने पर कुणित यानी मुड़ा हुआ या टेढ़ा होना।
english: The special point, however: gulpha—maṇibandha (wrist), and likewise jānu—kūrpara (elbow); in the piercing of those two, kuṇita (bentness, crookedness).

text_flags.why: possible: the line ends with a bare stem; line 17 (card 17) has 'kuṇitvaṃ' (crookedness) for the same effect

notes: Read as a correspondence: what is gulpha in the leg is maṇibandha in the arm, and jānu is kūrpara; the line itself only juxtaposes the names (no copula). 'jānukūrparaṃ' is split as jānu + kūrparam. 'kuṇita' is kept as printed (a participle 'bent'); whether kuṇitvam is meant does not change the sense. GROUPING: appears to continue 15.

words.gloss: armpit (kakṣā); akṣa (sense uncertain); in the middle

hindi: और विटप के समान, कक्षा यानी काँख और अक्ष, जिसका अर्थ अनिश्चित है, के बीच कक्षाधार; वहाँ कुणित्व यानी टेढ़ापन।
english: And like viṭapa: in the middle of the armpit (kakṣā) and the akṣa (sense uncertain), kakṣādhāra; there, kuṇitva (crookedness).

text_flags.why: possible: 'akṣa' is not a known body part (akṣaka would be the collar-bone); 'between the armpit and the chest (vakṣas)' is a plausible reading, v lost; not adopted in the translation

notes: 'like viṭapa' is read as the arm's counterpart of the groin marma in 14 (position between two parts, same kind of effect); not stated further. akṣa is left untranslated as uncertain. GROUPING: appears to continue 15-16 (arms).

words.gloss: wind (vāta); stool (varcas); expelling; thick; intestine; bound to

hindi: वायु और मल को बाहर निकालने वाली स्थूलान्त्र यानी बड़ी आँत से बँधा हुआ गुद यानी गुदा; वहाँ तुरन्त मृत्यु।
english: The guda (anus), bound to the large intestine (sthūlāntra), the expeller of wind (vāta) and stool (varcas); there, immediate death.
notes: In the compound it is not settled whether 'nirasana' (expelling) qualifies the guda or the sthūlāntra (large intestine); the translation keeps it with the intestine, as the compound order suggests. 'vāta' is read as wind (flatus). sthūlāntra = large intestine: standard. guda covers the anus and rectal end.

hindi: बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय: अल्प मांस और रक्त वाली, भीतर क्टचा जो अस्पष्ट छपा शब्द है, इसलिए अनुमानित पाठ पर, धनुष के समान टेढ़ी, एक द्वार वाली, नीचे की ओर मुख वाली; वहाँ भी तुरन्त मृत्यु, अश्मरी यानी मूत्र की पथरी के व्रण यानी घाव को छोड़कर।
english: The basti (urinary bladder): having little flesh and blood, internally kṭacā (an unclear printed word, so on a conjectural reading), bow-curved, with one opening, with its mouth turned downward; there too, immediate death, except from the wound of aśmarī (urinary stone).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kṭacā' is not a word (no vowel after k); 'abhyantarataḥ kaṭyāḥ' (inside the waist/hip) would suit the position of the bladder; 'tvacā' (with skin) is another candidate; not adopted

notes: The word kṭacā is damaged and kept unsplit; the sentence is therefore on a conjectural reading. The bladder is described by shape: little flesh and blood, bow-curved, one opening, mouth downward. 'aśmarī-vraṇa' = wound of/for urinary stone; the natural sense is the wound made to remove a stone, but the line does not say so. 'ṛte' takes the ablative. Here basti is the bladder. GROUPING: 20 appears to continue 19.
lines_deva: अल्पमांसशोणितोऽभ्यंतरतः क्टचा धनुर्वक्र एकद्वारोऽधोमुखो बस्तिः तत्रापि सद्यो मरणमश्मरीव्रणादृते
lines_iast: alpamāṃsaśoṇito'bhyaṃtarataḥ kṭacā dhanurvakra ekadvāro'dhomukho bastiḥ tatrāpi sadyo maraṇamaśmarīvraṇādṛte

hindi: वहाँ भी दोनों ओर बिंधने पर जीवित नहीं रहता; एक ओर फट जाने पर मूत्र बहाने वाला घाव होता है; वह प्रयत्न से उपचारित किया गया भर जाता है।
english: Even there, when pierced on both sides, one does not live; when split on one side, a wound discharging urine (mūtra) results; that, however, treated with effort, heals.
notes: The subject of 'jīvati' is unstated (the person); shown as 'one'. 'sa' is the wound. upakrānta = treated, taken in hand (treatment); rohati = grows over, heals. GROUPING: appears to continue 19 (the basti).
lines_deva: तत्राप्युभयतो विद्धे न जीवति एकतो भिन्ने मूत्रस्रावी व्रणो भवति स तु यत्नेनोपक्रांतो रोहति
lines_iast: tatrāpyubhayato viddhe na jīvati ekato bhinne mūtrasrāvī vraṇo bhavati sa tu yatnenopakrāṃto rohati

words.gloss: pakva (digested; with āśaya understood: pakvāśaya, probably the lower gut); āmāśaya (stomach; standard); in the middle

hindi: पक्व यानी पचे हुए और आमाशय यानी कच्चे अन्न के आशय, सम्भवतः जठर, के बीच नाभि; वहाँ भी तुरन्त मृत्यु।
english: In the middle of the pakva (digested) and the āmāśaya (probably the stomach), the nābhi (navel); there too, immediate death.

text_flags.why: possible: 'pakka' is the Prakrit form; the Sanskrit word is pakva; va/ka confusion in print

notes: 'pakva-āmāśaya' is a dvandva in which 'pakva' stands for pakvāśaya (the receptacle of digested matter, probably the lower gut); this is the usual sense but the word āśaya is not printed after pakva. āmāśaya = the receptacle of undigested food, the stomach (standard). Nominal sentence.

words.gloss: sattva, rajas, tamas (the three guṇas, qualities); seat

hindi: कोष्ठ यानी पेट और वक्ष के तथा दोनों स्तनों के बीच सत्त्व, रज और तम नामक तीन गुणों का आधार, आमाशय यानी सम्भवतः जठर का द्वार, हृदय; वहाँ भी तुरन्त मृत्यु।
english: In the middle of the koṣṭha (belly) and the chest (vakṣas), and of the two breasts, the hṛdaya (heart), the seat of sattva, rajas and tamas (the three guṇas, qualities), the gate of the āmāśaya (probably the stomach); there too, immediate death.

text_flags.why: avagraha dropped after -o (tamo 'dhiṣṭhāna); also madhye is run on to the next word

notes: 'satva' is a print spelling of sattva (normalised in `w`). The guṇas are doctrinal terms, kept with a short gloss. 'koṣṭha' is taken as the abdominal-trunk cavity; its relation to 'vakṣas' ('between belly and chest') is read as a dvandva in the genitive dual. Hindi 'आमाशय' is the Sanskrit word for the receptacle of undigested food, not the mango (आम).
lines_deva: कोष्ठवक्षसोः स्तनयोश्च मध्येसत्वरजस्तमोधिष्ठानमामाशयद्वारं हृदयं तत्रापि सद्यो मरणं
lines_iast: koṣṭhavakṣasoḥ stanayośca madhyesatvarajastamodhiṣṭhānamāmāśayadvāraṃ hṛdayaṃ tatrāpi sadyo maraṇaṃ

words.gloss: breast; root (name of the two marmas)

hindi: दोनों स्तनों के नीचे दो अंगुल, दोनों ओर, स्तनमूल; उन दोनों में कफ से भरे कोष्ठ वाले की मृत्यु।
english: Two aṅgulas below the two breasts, on both sides, the two stanamūla (breast-roots); in those two, death of one whose koṣṭha (belly) is full of Kapha.
notes: 'stanamūle' is a dual (the two marmas, one on each side). 'tayoḥ' is read as 'in those two (when pierced)'. The wording is 'of one whose koṣṭha is full of Kapha': death depends on that state; the text gives no more. No verb.
lines_deva: स्तनयोरधस्तात् द्व्यंगुलमुभयतः स्तनमूले तयोः कफपूर्णकोष्ठस्य मरणं
lines_iast: stanayoradhastāt dvyaṃgulamubhayataḥ stanamūle tayoḥ kaphapūrṇakoṣṭhasya maraṇaṃ

words.gloss: breast; rohita (name of the two marmas)

hindi: दोनों स्तनाग्रों के ऊपर दो अंगुल, दोनों ओर, स्तनरोहित; तुरन्त रक्त से भरे कोष्ठ वाले की मृत्यु।
english: Two aṅgulas above the two nipples (cūcuka), on both sides, the two stanarohita; immediate death of one whose koṣṭha (belly) is full of blood.

text_flags.why: possible: before ś the visarga is not changed to o; 'sadyaḥ' (or 'sadyaś') is expected

notes: Unlike 23 and 25 there is no 'tayoḥ' here; the effect is stated directly. 'stanacūcuka' is read as a dvandva (breast and nipple). The 'koṣṭha full of blood' wording parallels 23.
lines_deva: स्तनचूचुकयोरूर्ध्वं द्व्यंगुलमुभयतः स्तनरोहिते सद्यो शोणितपूर्णकोष्ठस्य मरणं
lines_iast: stanacūcukayorūrdhvaṃ dvyaṃgulamubhayataḥ stanarohite sadyo śoṇitapūrṇakoṣṭhasya maraṇaṃ

hindi: दोनों ओर छाती की दो नाड़ियाँ जो वात यानी वायु को ले जाती हैं, अपस्तम्भ; उन दोनों में रक्त से भरे कोष्ठ होने के कारण और कास यानी खाँसी तथा श्वास यानी सम्भवतः साँस फूलने से मृत्यु।
english: On both sides of the chest (uras), two nāḍī (channels) carrying vāta (wind), the two apastambha; in those two, death through the koṣṭha being full of blood, and through cough (kāsa) and śvāsa (probably breathlessness).
notes: 'vātavahe' could also mean carrying Vāta (the doṣa); 'wind' (breath, air) is the plainer sense for chest channels and is kept, with the Sanskrit word beside it. nāḍī is kept as 'channel, tube' (doctrinal vessel word). śvāsa = laboured breathing (breathlessness): probable; it is also a disease name.
lines_deva: उभयत्रोरसो नाड्यौ वातवहे अपस्तंभौ तयोःशोणितपूर्णकोष्ठतया कासश्वासाभ्यां च मरणं
lines_iast: ubhayatroraso nāḍyau vātavahe apastaṃbhau tayoḥśoṇitapūrṇakoṣṭhatayā kāsaśvāsābhyāṃ ca maraṇaṃ

hindi: दोनों अंसकूट यानी कन्धे के शिखरों के नीचे, दोनों पार्श्वों के भागों के ऊपर, अपालाप; उन दोनों में पूय यानी मवाद की अवस्था को प्राप्त हुए रक्त से मृत्यु।
english: Below the two aṃsakūṭa (shoulder-tops), above the parts of the two sides (pārśva), the two apālāpa; in those two, death by blood that has turned into pus (pūya).
notes: 'pārśvayor upari bhāgayoḥ' is read as 'above the parts of the two sides'; the exact relation of 'bhāgayoḥ' to the flanks is not firm (it could be 'above, in the portions of the sides'). aṃsakūṭa = top of the shoulder (probable: the acromion region). No verb.
lines_deva: अंसकूटयोरधः पार्श्वयोरुपरि भागयोरपालापौ तयोः पूयत्वमापन्नेन रक्तेन मरणं
lines_iast: aṃsakūṭayoradhaḥ pārśvayorupari bhāgayorapālāpau tayoḥ pūyatvamāpannena raktena maraṇaṃ

hindi: रीढ़ यानी पृष्ठवंश के दोनों ओर श्रोणिकर्णों की ओर दो अस्थियाँ, कटीकतरुण; उन दोनों में रक्त के क्षय से पाण्डु यानी फीका सफेद, विवर्ण यानी बदरंग और क्षीण रूप वाला मरता है।
english: On both sides of the spine (pṛṣṭhavaṃśa), towards the two śroṇīkarṇa (hip-'ears'), two bones, the kaṭīkataruṇa; in those two, from loss of blood (śoṇita), one dies pale (pāṇḍu), discoloured (vivarṇa) and of diminished appearance.
notes: 'prati' + accusative is read as 'towards'. śroṇīkarṇa (hip-ear) names a part of the pelvic region (it occurs again in 29); its exact structure is not firm. kaṭīkataruṇa is kept as a marma name. The subject of 'mriyate' is unstated (the person). Hindi pāṇḍu: 'pale' (the glossary's open point on the Hindi word).
lines_deva: पृष्ठवंशमुभयतः प्रतिश्रोणीकर्णावस्थिनी कटीकतरुणे तयोः शोणितक्षयात् पांडुर्विवर्णो हीनरूपो म्रियते
lines_iast: pṛṣṭhavaṃśamubhayataḥ pratiśroṇīkarṇāvasthinī kaṭīkataruṇe tayoḥ śoṇitakṣayāt pāṃḍurvivarṇo hīnarūpo mriyate

words.gloss: touch; non-perception (on a conjectural reading; printed sparśa-jñānam)

hindi: दोनों पार्श्वों में जघन यानी सम्भवतः कूल्हे के क्षेत्र के बाहरी भाग में, रीढ़ के दोनों ओर, कुकुन्दर; उन दोनों में निचले शरीर में स्पर्श का अज्ञान यानी अनुभव न होना, अनुमानित पाठ पर, और चेष्टा का नाश यानी हिलने-डुलने की हानि।
english: On the two sides, in the outer part of the jaghana (probably the hip region), on both sides of the spine, the two kukundara; in those two, absence of perception of touch (sparśa-ajñāna) in the lower body, on a conjectural reading, and loss of movement (ceṣṭā).

text_flags.why: possible: as printed, 'knowledge of touch' would be a good thing among a list of harms; the long ā of sparśājñāna (absence of knowing touch) is a likely slip

notes: The conjecture 'sparśājñāna' is marked in both translations. A second possibility is that a word for 'loss' (nāśa) has dropped after sparśajñāna, giving the same sense. jaghana = hips or loins region: probable. ceṣṭā = movement, bodily activity.
lines_deva: पार्श्वयोर्जघनबहिर्भागे पृष्ठवंशमुभयतः कुकुंदरौ तयोः स्पर्शज्ञानमधःकाये चेष्टानाशश्च
lines_iast: pārśvayorjaghanabahirbhāge pṛṣṭhavaṃśamubhayataḥ kukuṃdarau tayoḥ sparśajñānamadhaḥkāye ceṣṭānāśaśca

words.gloss: nitamba (marma name, two; the word means hip or buttock)

hindi: दोनों श्रोणिकर्णों के ऊपर, आशय को ढकने वाले और पार्श्वों के भीतरी भाग से बँधे, नितम्ब; उन दोनों में निचले शरीर में सूजन, दुर्बलता और मृत्यु।
english: Above the two śroṇīkarṇa (hip-'ears'), the two nitamba, covering the āśaya (receptacle) and bound to the interior of the sides (pārśva-antara); in those two, swelling (śopha) and weakness in the lower body, and death.

text_flags.why: possible: pārśva + antara gives pārśvāntara with long ā; the long mark looks dropped (also in 30)
near certain: the full stop stands for the visarga (adhaḥ-kāye)

notes: 'āśaya' is left as 'receptacle' (an unspecified internal space); the line does not name the organ. 'pārśvāntara' is read as the interior (interval) of the sides; the sense of 'antara' here is not firm. 'ācchādana' = covering.
lines_deva: श्रोणीकर्णयोरुपर्याशयाच्छादनौ पार्श्वन्तरप्रतिबद्धौ नितंबौ तयोरध.काये शोफो दौर्बल्यं मरणं च
lines_iast: śroṇīkarṇayoruparyāśayācchādanau pārśvantarapratibaddhau nitaṃbau tayoradha.kāye śopho daurbalyaṃ maraṇaṃ ca

words.gloss: side; joint (name of the two marmas)

hindi: नीचे पार्श्वों के भीतरी भाग से बँधे, जघन यानी सम्भवतः कूल्हे का क्षेत्र और पार्श्व के बीच तिरछे और ऊपर की ओर, पार्श्वसन्धि; उन दोनों में रक्त से भरे कोष्ठ होने के कारण मृत्यु।
english: Bound to the lower interior of the sides, in the middle between the jaghana (probably the hip region) and the side (pārśva), slanting and upward, the two pārśvasandhi (side-joints); in those two, death through the koṣṭha being full of blood.

text_flags.why: possible: long ā of pārśvāntara dropped, as in 29

notes: 'tiryagūrdhvam ca' is read as the direction of the marmas ('slanting and upward'), not as a separate marma. As in 29, 'pārśvāntara' = interior of the sides (sense of antara not firm).
lines_deva: अधःपार्श्वन्तरप्रतिबद्धौ जघनपार्श्वमध्ये तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च पार्श्वसंधी तयोः शोणितपूर्णकोष्ठतया मरणं
lines_iast: adhaḥpārśvantarapratibaddhau jaghanapārśvamadhye tiryagūrdhvaṃ ca pārśvasaṃdhī tayoḥ śoṇitapūrṇakoṣṭhatayā maraṇaṃ

words.gloss: by straightness, in a straight line
bṛhatī (marma name, two; the word means 'large')

hindi: दोनों स्तनमूलों से सीधी रेखा में, रीढ़ के दोनों ओर, बृहती; उन दोनों में रक्त के अतिप्रवाह से उत्पन्न उपद्रवों यानी जटिलताओं से मृत्यु।
english: In a straight line (ārjava) with the two stanamūla, on both sides of the spine, the two bṛhatī; in those two, death through complications (upadrava) whose cause is an excessive flow of blood.
notes: Printed 'ārjjava' (doubled jj) is normalised to ārjava (print habit). The literal wording is 'by straightness' from the two stanamūla; 'in a straight line with' is the plain sense. bṛhatī here is a marma name, not the plant. upadrava = complication, secondary affliction.

words.gloss: shoulder (aṃsa); plate (phalaka) (the two shoulder-blades, scapulae; probable)

hindi: रीढ़ के दोनों ओर, बाहु के मूल से जुड़े, अंसफलक यानी कन्धे की दो फलकें, सम्भवतः स्कन्धास्थियाँ; उन दोनों में भुजा का स्वाप यानी सुन्न होना और शोष यानी सूखकर क्षीण होना।
english: On both sides of the spine, the two aṃsaphalaka (shoulder-plates, probably the shoulder-blades), joined to the roots of the arms; in those two, numbness (svāpa) and wasting (śoṣa) of the arm.
notes: The line has 'bāhu' only once in the last compound ('arm-numbness and arm-wasting' or 'numbness and wasting of the arm'); the second is kept. aṃsaphalaka = shoulder-blade: probable. svāpa = numbness, loss of feeling (it can also mean sleep). No verb.

words.gloss: neck; arm; head; in the middle

hindi: ग्रीवा, बाहु और शिर के बीच अंसपीठ और स्कन्ध को बाँधने वाले दो अंस यानी कन्धे; उन दोनों में भुजा की अकड़न।
english: In the middle of the neck, arm and head, the two aṃsa (shoulders), binders of the aṃsapīṭha (shoulder-seat) and the skandha (shoulder-top); in those two, stiffness of the arms.

text_flags.why: possible: 'asapīṭha' is not a word; the anusvara of aṃsapīṭha looks dropped

notes: skandha = shoulder, the top of the back or shoulder (sense of the pair aṃsapīṭha / skandha not firm). The compound after the avagraha is read as 'binding aṃsapīṭha and skandha'. stabdhabāhutā = the state of having stiff arms.

hindi: कण्ठनाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः श्वासनली के दोनों ओर चार धमनियाँ यानी वाहिकाएँ; उनमें दो नीला, दो मन्या; उनमें मूकता यानी गूँगापन, स्वर का विकार, अथवा रस का ग्रहण न कर पाना होता है।
english: On both sides of the kaṇṭha-nāḍī (throat-tube, probably the windpipe), four dhamanī (vessels); of these, two nīlā, two manyā; in those, dumbness (mūkatā), alteration of the voice, or inability to perceive taste (rasa) occurs.
notes: dhamanī is a doctrinal word for a vessel and is kept with a plain gloss, not forced into 'artery'. nīlā and manyā are taken as names (nīla = blue; manyā = neck/nape); this is not firm: nīle could be an adjective 'blue' and manye a name. The three signs are alternatives ('or', singular verb). rasa here is taste.
lines_deva: कंठनाडीमुभयतश्चतस्त्रो धमन्यः तासां द्वे नीले द्वे मन्ये तासु मूकता स्वरवैकृत्यं रसाग्राहिता वा भवति
lines_iast: kaṃṭhanāḍīmubhayataścatastro dhamanyaḥ tāsāṃ dve nīle dve manye tāsu mūkatā svaravaikṛtyaṃ rasāgrāhitā vā bhavati

hindi: ग्रीवा में दोनों ओर चार सिराएँ यानी वाहिकाएँ, मातृका; उनमें तुरन्त मृत्यु।
english: In the neck, on both sides, four sirā (vessels), the mātṛkā; in those, immediate death.
notes: Printed 'sirā mātṛkāḥ' = sirāḥ mātṛkāḥ (regular loss of visarga before a voiced consonant). sirā is a doctrinal vessel word, kept with a plain gloss (it is usually rendered 'vein', not forced here). Nominal sentence.

words.gloss: kṛkāṭikā (name, two; the nape joints, probable)
vidhura (name of a marma; word means bereft, shaken)

hindi: शिर और ग्रीवा के जोड़ पर कृकाटिका; उन दोनों में शिर की चंचलता यानी डगमगाना। कानों के पीछे के भाग के नीचे स्थित दो विधुर नामक मर्म; उन दोनों का बहरापन।
english: At the junction of head and neck, the two kṛkāṭikā; in those two, an unsteady head (cala-mūrdha-tā). The two vidhura (marmas) situated below the backs of the two ears: of those two, deafness (bādhirya).
notes: [02.07.36] Printed 'mūrddha' (doubled dd) normalised to mūrdha. kṛkāṭikā = the nape joints (probable: the junction of the neck and skull). cala = moving, unsteady, shaky. [02.07.37] Elliptical: no verb is printed and none is supplied. 'Vidhura' is a marma (vital spot) name; the injury that causes the deafness is understood, not stated. The sentence is read as a heading plus result.

words.gloss: phaṇa (name of a marma; word means hood)

hindi: नाक के मार्ग के दोनों ओर, भीतर की ओर कान के मार्ग से जुड़े हुए दो फण नामक मर्म; उन दोनों का गन्ध का ज्ञान न होना।
english: On both sides of the nose-passage, on the inside, bound to the ear-passage, the two phaṇa (marmas): of those two, non-perception of smell.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is printed and none is supplied. The print joins 'abhyantarataḥ' and 'phaṇau' without a space (spacing slip). Whether 'ubhayataḥ' goes with the nose-passage or with the phaṇas is not settled; the plainest reading is kept. Injury is understood, not stated. The printed 'pratibaddham' is singular, so it does not agree with the dual 'phaṇau'; it may go with 'ghrāṇamārgam' (the nose-passage is joined to the ear-passage) or be a slip for a dual. The translation keeps the reading that the phaṇas are joined to the ear-passage (plainest sense); not settled.

words.gloss: apāṅga (name of a marma; the outer corner of the eye, probable)

hindi: दोनों भौंहों के पूँछ-छोरों के नीचे, दोनों आँखों के बाहर की ओर दो अपाङ्ग नामक मर्म; उन दोनों का अन्धापन।
english: Below the tail-ends of the two brows, on the outside of the two eyes, the two apāṅga (marmas): of those two, blindness (āndhya).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is printed and none is supplied. 'puccha-anta' = the tapering tail-end of the brow. Identification of apāṅga with the outer corner of the eye: probable (the word itself means 'outer corner of the eye' in ordinary Sanskrit). Injury is understood, not stated.

words.gloss: śaṅkha (name of a marma; the temple, probable)
in the two low places, hollows
āvarta (name of a marma; word means whorl, eddy)

hindi: दोनों भौंहों के पूँछ-छोरों के ऊपर, कान की ओर, माथे पर दो शङ्ख नामक मर्म यानी सम्भवतः कनपटियाँ; उन दोनों का तत्काल मरण। भौंहों के ऊपर दो गड्ढों में दो आवर्त नामक मर्म; उन दोनों का अन्धापन या दृष्टि की हानि।
english: Above the tail-ends of the two brows, toward the ear, on the forehead, the two śaṅkha (marmas, probably the temples): of those two, death at once. Above the two brows, in the two hollows, the two āvarta (marmas): of those two, blindness or damage to sight.
notes: [02.07.40] Elliptical: no verb is printed and none is supplied. 'utkarṇam' is taken as 'toward the ear'; this sense is probable, not certain. śaṅkha = temple region of the head: probable (the ordinary meaning of the word is 'conch', and 'temple' by shape). Injury is understood, not stated. [02.07.41] Elliptical: no verb is printed and none is supplied. 'nimnayoḥ' (locative dual) is read with the āvartas as 'in the two hollows'. Injury is understood, not stated.
lines_deva: भ्रुवोः पुच्छांतयोरुपर्युत्कर्णं ललाटे शंखौ तयोः सद्यो मरणं
lines_iast: bhruvoḥ pucchāṃtayoruparyutkarṇaṃ lalāṭe śaṃkhau tayoḥ sadyo maraṇaṃ

words.gloss: utkṣepa (name of a marma; word means throwing up)

hindi: दोनों शङ्खों के ऊपर केशों के छोर पर दो उत्क्षेप नामक मर्म; उन दोनों में शल्य सहित, या पाक यानी पक जाने से जिसका शल्य गिर गया हो, वह जी सकता है; जिसका शल्य निकाल दिया गया हो वह नहीं।
english: Above the two śaṅkhas, at the hair-ends, the two utkṣepa (marmas): of those two, one with the dart (śalya) still in, or one whose dart has fallen out through suppuration (pāka), may live; not one whose dart has been pulled out.
notes: 'keśāntau' is dual and agrees with utkṣepau: 'the two utkṣepas at the hair-margin'. 'Of those two' = in the case of injury to those two (understood). The word śalya (dart, any piercing object) is kept as 'dart'. 'pāka' = ripening, suppuration. The unstated subject is shown as 'one'.
lines_deva: शंखयोरुपरि केशांतउत्क्षेपौ तयोः सशल्यः पाकात्पतितशल्यो वा जीवेन्नोद्धृतशल्यः
lines_iast: śaṃkhayorupari keśāṃtautkṣepau tayoḥ saśalyaḥ pākātpatitaśalyo vā jīvennoddhṛtaśalyaḥ

words.gloss: sthapanī (name of a marma; word means support, a stand)

hindi: दोनों भौंहों के बीच स्थपनी नामक मर्म; वहाँ उत्क्षेप के समान।
english: In the middle of the two brows, the sthapanī (marma); there, as with the utkṣepa.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is printed and none is supplied. 'tatra utkṣepavat' = in the same way as stated for the utkṣepas (the result of injury, as in the preceding unit); the effect is not restated here. Not enriched.

words.gloss: sīmanta (name of a marma; word means parting of the hair)

hindi: सिर पर तिरछे और ऊपर की ओर पाँच सन्धियाँ सीमन्त नामक हैं; उनमें उन्माद, चक्कर आने और चित्त के नाश से मरण।
english: Five joints (sandhi) on the head, transverse and upward, called sīmanta (marmas): in those, death by way of insanity (unmāda), giddiness (bhrama) and loss of mind (citta-nāśa).
notes: The five sandhi of the head are probably the sutures of the skull (probable, not stated). 'sīmantā nāma' is regular sandhi for sīmantāḥ nāma. The instrumental is read as 'by way of' (the signs through which death comes). Whether 'tiryak' and 'ūrdhvam' describe the direction of the joints is the plainest reading; not enriched.
lines_deva: पंच संधयः शिरसितिर्यगूर्ध्वं च सीमंता नाम तेषून्मादभ्रमचित्तनाशैर्मरणं
lines_iast: paṃca saṃdhayaḥ śirasitiryagūrdhvaṃ ca sīmaṃtā nāma teṣūnmādabhramacittanāśairmaraṇaṃ

hindi: जीभ, नाक, आँख और कान को तृप्त करने वाली सिराओं का तालु में मिलन; उनके चार मुख शृङ्गाटक नाम वाले हैं; उनमें तत्काल मरण।
english: Of the vessels (sirā) that satiate the tongue, nose, eye and ear, the meeting is in the palate (tālu); their four mouths are named śṛṅgāṭaka; in those, death at once.
notes: Printed 'jivhā' = jihvā (accepted spelling variant; no flag). 'tarpaṇa' = satiation (glossary). sirā is kept as 'vessel (sirā)'; no single modern vessel is named. 'śṛṅgāṭaka' = marma name (the word means a triangle or junction). Verbless clauses are left without a verb.
lines_deva: जिव्हाघ्राणाक्षिश्रोत्रतर्पणीनां सिराणां तालुनि सन्निपातः तासां मुखानि चत्वारि शृंगाटकसंज्ञानि तेषु सद्यो मरणं
lines_iast: jivhāghrāṇākṣiśrotratarpaṇīnāṃ sirāṇāṃ tāluni sannipātaḥ tāsāṃ mukhāni catvāri śṛṃgāṭakasaṃjñāni teṣu sadyo maraṇaṃ

words.gloss: adhipati (name of a marma; word means overlord)

hindi: सिर के भीतर, ऊपर की ओर, सिराओं और सन्धियों का मिलन, जो बालों का भँवर है; वह अधिपति नामक है; वहाँ भी तत्काल मरण होता है।
english: Inside the head, above, the meeting of vessels (śirā) and joints (sandhi), a whorl of hair: that is called adhipati; there too death occurs at once.
notes: The print joins 'mastakābhyantaram' and 'upariṣṭāt' without a space (spacing slip). The closing 'iti' marks the end of the passage and is not translated. 'śirā' = sirā (spelling variant). 'roma-āvarta' = hair-whorl, read as describing the spot.
lines_deva: मस्तकाभ्यंतरंउपरिष्टाच्छिरासंधिसन्निपातो रोमावर्तः सोऽधिपतिर्नाम तत्रापि सद्यो मरणं भवतीति
lines_iast: mastakābhyaṃtaraṃupariṣṭācchirāsaṃdhisannipāto romāvartaḥ so'dhipatirnāma tatrāpi sadyo maraṇaṃ bhavatīti

hindi: फिर मर्मों का सामान्य लक्षण: पीड़ित होने पर पीड़ा की उत्पत्ति और अनियमित स्पन्दन।
english: Further, the general sign of the marmas: when pressed (or injured), arising of pain and irregular throbbing.
notes: 'pīḍite' (locative, 'when pressed') is impersonal; the injured marma is understood. Verbless sentence, no verb supplied. 'punar' is read as 'further' (a new topic).
lines_deva: सामान्यलक्षणं पुनर्मर्मणां पीडिते रुजोत्पत्तिर्विषमं च स्पंदनं
lines_iast: sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ punarmarmaṇāṃ pīḍite rujotpattirviṣamaṃ ca spaṃdanaṃ

hindi: और सामान्य से ही।
english: And by the general (one) alone.
notes: Elliptical. GROUPING: appears to continue 47 and to introduce the list in 49-50 (the noun, probably 'sign', is not printed and is not supplied; 'by' may also mean 'in general'). Not enriched.

hindi: देहप्रमुसि जो अस्पष्ट है, भारीपन, सम्मोह यानी भ्रम और शीत की इच्छा। पसीना आना, मूर्च्छा, वमन और श्वास का कष्ट: मर्म में बिंधे हुए का लक्षण।
english: Dehapramusi (unclear), heaviness (gurutā), bewilderment (saṃmoha), desire for cold (śīta-kāmitā). Sweating, fainting (mūrcchā), vomiting and breathlessness (śvāsa): the sign of one pierced in a marma.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dehapramusi' is not a known word; it may be a damaged word for a body symptom of the same kind (for example numbness, dehaprasupti, or similar); no restoration is adopted

notes: [02.07.49] The first word is damaged or unknown: it is kept unsplit as printed, glossed unclear, and left untranslated; any guess stays out of the translation. The rest are signs listed in the nominative (verbless). Together with 50 this forms a list of signs; 50 closes it with 'sign of one pierced in a marma'. [02.07.50] 'vamiḥ' (vami, vomiting) is an accepted form; no flag. 'śvāsa' is breathing trouble in general (dyspnoea is the usual modern sense: probable). The four items are read as a list in the nominative with 'lakṣaṇam' as the predicate noun (no verb printed).

hindi: और भी।
english: And further.
notes: Connective formula introducing the next statement; GROUPING: opens 52.

words.gloss: flesh; vessel; sinew; bone; joint; meeting

hindi: मरण कराने के कारण मर्म; और वह मांस, सिरा, स्नायु, अस्थि और सन्धि का मिलन।
english: Because of causing death, marma; and that, moreover, the meeting of flesh, vessels, sinews, bone and joint.
notes: Verbless; no verb supplied. Printed 'snāva' = sinew (snāyu); both forms occur. 'sandhi' (joint) is taken as the fifth item of the dvandva; whether it could be 'bone-joint' is not decided by the wording. The text's own explanation of the word; no etymology is added.

hindi: इसलिए उसके पीड़ित होने पर विशेष रूप से प्राण को बाधा।
english: Therefore, when that is being pressed (or injured), especially affliction of the life-breath (prāṇa).
notes: Verbless; no verb supplied. 'prāṇa' = vital breath, life; kept as 'life-breath (prāṇa)'.

words.gloss: by abundance, for the most part

hindi: किन्तु निर्देश बाहुल्य से।
english: But the designation: by preponderance (bāhulya).
notes: Verbless; no verb supplied. Sense: the name 'marma' is given according to what predominates, not as an exact rule; this is interpretation and kept out of the translation.

words.gram: first member of the compound continued in the next token

hindi: इसलिए अनुमानित पाठ पर मांस आदि के आश्रय के अनुसार मर्म पाँच प्रकार से विभक्त होते हैं।
english: Therefore, on a conjectural reading, according to their basis in flesh and the rest, the marmas are divided in five ways.

text_flags.why: possible: 'māṃ sādyā-' looks like a stray space inside māṃsādi-āśrayataḥ; the following units (57-61) list flesh, sinew, bone, joint marmas, which fits 'flesh and the rest'

notes: Conjectural reading: 'māṃsādyāśrayataḥ' = 'by the basis in flesh etc.' (the word is split across two printed tokens, so the split of 'tasmānmāṃ' gives only the first part). The five types are named in the units that follow (not stated here).

hindi: वह इस प्रकार है।
english: That is as follows.
notes: Introductory formula; the list begins in 57.

words.gloss: talahṛdaya (marma name; centre of palm or sole, probable)
indrabasti (marma name; mid-calf or mid-forearm region, probable)

hindi: तलहृदय, इन्द्रबस्ति, गुद यानी मलद्वार और स्तनरोहित: ग्यारह मांस-मर्म।
english: Talahṛdaya, indrabasti, guda (anus, rectum) and stanarohita: eleven flesh-marmas (māṃsa-marma).
notes: Verbless list; no verb supplied. The fivefold division announced in 55 begins here (flesh marmas). 'Stanarohita' is read as one name, not as 'stana' and 'rohita' separately; the split is probable. Identifications of the marma names with body regions: probable (the names are standard marma names; regions come from the commentarial tradition, not from this line). The count 'eleven' is translated as printed. COUNT CHECK (observation, from this book's own limb and trunk units): eleven = talahṛdaya 4 + indrabasti 4 (one per limb, lines 4 and 9 (card 4/9)) + guda 1 (u18) + stanarohita 2 (u24). The printed number counts every side and limb, not the number of names.

words.gloss: stana (breast); first member of stanamūla, continued in the next token
manyā (marma name; on a conjectural reading, printed 'manmā')

hindi: उर्वी, लोहिताख्य, नाभि, हृदय, स्तनमूल, अपस्तम्भ, अलाप, पार्श्वसन्धि, बृहती, नीला, अनुमानित पाठ पर मन्या, मातृका, फण, अपाङ्ग, स्थपनी और शृङ्गाटक: इकतालीस सिरा-मर्म।
english: Urvī, lohitākhya, nābhi (navel), hṛdaya (heart), stanamūla, apastambha, alāpa, pārśvasandhi, bṛhatī, nīlā, manyā (on a conjectural reading), mātṛkā, phaṇa, apāṅga, sthapanī and śṛṅgāṭaka: forty-one vessel-marmas (sirā-marma).

text_flags.why: possible: 'manmā' is not a marma name; 'manyā' (the neck marma) is the usual name between nīlā and mātṛkā, and ya -> n+m is a plausible OCR error (also seen in 67 'nīlāmandyā')
possible: 'alāpa' is probably apālāpa (printed 'apālāpau' in u26); the syllable pā was lost after apastambha; kept as printed in the split and not adopted in the translation

notes: Verbless list. Printed 'stana mūla' (space inside the compound) = stanamūla, a spacing slip. 'lohitākhya' = 'called lohita' (a marma name); 'urvī' as in 67. Printed 'śirā' = sirā (variant). Marma names are kept untranslated; nābhi and hṛdaya are also ordinary words for navel and heart, so the equivalents are given as standard. The count 'forty-one' is translated as printed. 'mātṛkā' and 'bṛhatī' kept as names. The emended manyā is conjectural and marked so in both translations. COUNT CHECK (observation): forty-one = urvī 4 + lohitākhya 4 (one per limb) + nābhi 1 + hṛdaya 1 + stanamūla 2 + apastambha 2 + alāpa (apālāpa) 2 + pārśvasandhi 2 + bṛhatī 2 + nīlā 2 + manyā 2 + mātṛkā 8 + phaṇa 2 + apāṅga 2 + sthapanī 1 + śṛṅgāṭaka 4, counting sides and limbs as in lines 4-46 (card 4/44). The 'alāpa' of this unit is probably the apālāpa of u26 (a lost pā).

words.gloss: kūrcaśiras (marma name; head of the kūrca)
kakṣādhara (marma name; kakṣa = armpit); āṇi (marma name)

hindi: क्षिप्र, कूर्च, कूर्चशिरस्, विटप, कक्षाधर, आणि, बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय, अंस यानी कन्धा, विधुर और उत्क्षेप: सत्ताईस स्नायु-मर्म।
english: Kṣipra, kūrca, kūrcaśiras, viṭapa, kakṣādhara, āṇi, basti (bladder), aṃsa (shoulder), vidhura and utkṣepa: twenty-seven sinew-marmas (snāva-marma).
notes: Verbless list. The print runs the whole list into one token ; it is read as a single dvandva list of names. 'kakṣādharāṇi' is read as kakṣādhara + āṇi (āṇi is the marma of u11), not as a neuter plural: with āṇi the printed total twenty-seven works out (kṣipra 4, kūrca 4, kūrcaśiras 4, āṇi 4, viṭapa 2, kakṣādhara 2, basti 1, aṃsa 2, vidhura 2, utkṣepa 2, counting limbs and sides as in lines 4-36 (card 4/36)); the single counts are not printed here. 'snāva' = sinew (snāyu). Here 'basti' is a marma name; its ordinary meaning (bladder, standard) is given beside it. The count 'twenty-seven' is translated as printed.

words.gloss: kaṭīkataruṇa (marma name; kaṭī = hip, loin; taruṇa also means cartilage, soft bone)
nitamba (marma name; buttock, hip, standard word)

hindi: कटीकतरुण, नितम्ब, अंसफलक यानी सम्भवतः कन्धे की चपटी हड्डियाँ और शङ्ख यानी सम्भवतः कनपटियाँ: आठ अस्थि-मर्म।
english: Kaṭīkataruṇa, nitamba, aṃsaphalaka (probably the shoulder-blades) and śaṅkha (probably the temples), however: eight bone-marmas (asthi-marma).
notes: Verbless list, one printed token. 'tu' is taken as a mild contrast with the preceding list. The count 'eight' is as printed; the names are kept as marma names, the equivalents in the glosses are probable.

words.gloss: kukundara (marma name; hollow of the buttock-loin region, probable)
kṛkāṭikā (marma name; joint at the back of the neck, probable)

hindi: गुल्फ यानी टखना, मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई, जानु यानी घुटना, कूर्पर यानी कोहनी, कुकुन्दर, कृकाटिका, आवर्त, सीमन्त और अधिपति: बीस सन्धि-मर्म।
english: Gulpha (ankle), maṇibandha (wrist), jānu (knee), kūrpara (elbow), kukundara, kṛkāṭikā, āvarta, sīmanta and adhipati: twenty joint-marmas (sandhi-marma).
notes: Verbless list. The double avagraha in 'kṛkāṭikā''varta' is a print habit (kṛkāṭikā + āvarta); no flag. The ending -adhipatayo (adhipatayaḥ; the visarga becomes o before the voiced v- of viṃśati by regular sandhi) is plural although the list ends on a single name; the plural is kept as printed. The count 'twenty' is translated as printed.

words.gloss: stana (marma name as printed; breast; reading doubtful, see flag)

hindi: फिर पाँच प्रकार से: गुदब जो अस्पष्ट है, स्तन जिसका पाठ सन्दिग्ध है, नाभि, हृदय, मातृका, शङ्ख, शृङ्गाटक और अधिपति: उन्नीस जो तत्काल प्राण हर लेते हैं; आग्नेय होने से उनका समय समरात्र जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है, उसके भीतर।
english: And again, in five ways: gudaba (unclear), stana (reading doubtful), nābhi (navel), hṛdaya (heart), mātṛkā, śaṅkha, śṛṅgāṭaka and adhipati: nineteen that take life at once; because of their fiery nature (āgneya), the time for them is within a samarātra (unclear).

text_flags.suggest: gudabasti (and stanābhi as stinābhi, i.e. gudabasti-nābhi)
text_flags.why: possible: 'gudaba' is not a word; 'gudaba stanābhi...' probably stands for gudabasti-nābhi-hṛdaya-... (the Devanagari 'गुदब स्तनाभि' = गुदबस्तिनाभि with a lost vowel sign); the nineteen then add up without any 'stana' marma (see notes); not adopted in the translation
possible: 'samarātra' is not a known word; pta/ma confusion would give saptarātra (seven nights); not adopted, the word is left unclear

notes: The first word of the list is damaged: kept unsplit as 'gudaba', glossed unclear, and left untranslated; the conjecture (guda and basti) is given only in the flag. The count 'nineteen' is as printed and the reader cannot check it against the damaged list. 'punaś ca pañcadhā' opens a second fivefold division (by effect on life); the five kinds are the headings of 62, 63, 65, 67 and 70 (this is an observation of the layout, not stated in this unit). 'samarātra' is not a known word and is left unclear in both translations; it may be a misprint of saptarātra ('seven nights', pta/ma confusion), which would suit the sequence with 'within a fortnight' in 63 (possible only; no sense is adopted). 'āgneya' = of Agni (fire). COUNT CHECK (observation, from this book's own units): nineteen = guda 1 (u18) + basti 1 (u19) + nābhi 1 (u21) + hṛdaya 1 (u22) + mātṛkā 8 (u35) + śaṅkha 2 (u40) + śṛṅgāṭaka 4 (u45) + adhipati 1 (u46). So the damaged start 'gudaba stanābhi' probably hides gudabasti and nābhi, and 'stana' is probably not a marma here; the printed text is kept and not corrected.
lines_deva: पुनश्च पंचधा गुदब स्तनाभिहृदयमातृकाशंखशृंगाटकाधिपतयएकोनविंशति सद्यः प्राणहराण्याग्नेयत्वात्तेषां समरात्राभ्यंतरं कालः
lines_iast: punaśca paṃcadhā gudaba stanābhihṛdayamātṛkāśaṃkhaśṛṃgāṭakādhipatayaekonaviṃśati sadyaḥ prāṇaharāṇyāgneyatvātteṣāṃ samarātrābhyaṃtaraṃ kālaḥ

hindi: तलहृदय, क्षिप्र, इन्द्रबस्ति, वक्षोमर्म जिसका पाठ सन्दिग्ध है, कटीकतरुण, नितम्ब, पार्श्वसन्धि, बृहती और सीमन्त: तैंतीस जो कालान्तर में प्राण हरते हैं; सौम्य और आग्नेय होने से उनका समय पक्ष के भीतर।
english: Talahṛdaya, kṣipra, indrabasti, vakṣomarma (reading doubtful), kaṭīkataruṇa, nitamba, pārśvasandhi, bṛhatī and sīmanta: thirty-three that take life after an interval; because of their being saumya (soft, of Soma) and fiery (āgneya), the time for them is within a fortnight (pakṣa).

text_flags.why: possible: 'vakṣomarma' (chest + marma) sits oddly inside a list of marma names; a name may have been lost or 'marma' may be stray; no restoration is adopted

notes: 'kālāntara' = after an interval of time. The print splits the list across two tokens at 'nitamba' / 'pārśvasandhi'. The count 'thirty-three' is as printed. 'saumya' = of Soma, soft, cool (the contrast with āgneya, fiery). Verbless, no verb supplied. 'vakṣomarma' is kept as printed. COUNT CHECK (observation, from this book's own units): the named marmas give talahṛdaya 4 + kṣipra 4 + indrabasti 4 + kaṭīkataruṇa 2 + nitamba 2 + pārśvasandhi 2 + bṛhatī 2 + sīmanta 5 = 25; the chest marmas of lines 23-26 (card 23/26) (stanamūla, stanarohita, apastambha, apālāpa, two each) make 8, giving exactly the printed thirty-three. So 'vakṣomarma' may be genuine, a collective 'chest marmas', and the flag may be unnecessary; kept as printed and left open.

hindi: उनमें भी किन्तु क्षिप्र नामक कभी शीघ्र।
english: Even among those, however, the kṣipra (ones), sometimes quickly.
notes: Elliptical: the verb is carried from 63 (taking life) and is not supplied. Read with 63; GROUPING: appears to continue 63.

hindi: दोनों उत्क्षेप और स्थपनी: तीन विशल्यघ्न यानी शल्य निकलने पर मारने वाले, वायु के स्वभाव के कारण।
english: The two utkṣepas and the sthapanī: three viśalyaghna (killing when freed from the dart), because of their nature of Vāyu (wind).
notes: Verbless; no verb supplied. 'viśalya' = without a dart (freed of it); the compound is read as 'killing the one freed of the dart', explained in 66. The earlier line 42 (card 40) says that an utkṣepa case may live with the dart in. 'vāyavya' = belonging to Vāyu (wind).

hindi: क्योंकि जब तक यहाँ शल्य के मुख से रुका हुआ वायु ठहरता है, तब तक वह जीता है।
english: For as long as Vāyu (wind), blocked at the mouth of the dart, stays here, so long (he) lives.
notes: 'avaruddhaḥ' could instead qualify the unstated person ('blocked by the dart's mouth'); it is taken with Vāyu as the plainer reading. The subject of 'jīvati' is not printed; 'he' is supplied only in the English as a pronoun.

words.gloss: kūrpara (marma name; elbow, standard); āṇi (marma name)
manyā (marma name; on a conjectural reading, printed 'mandyā')

hindi: कूर्च, जानु, कूर्पर, आणि, उर्वी, लोहिताख्य, विटप, कक्षाधर, कुकुन्दर, अंसफलक, नीला, अनुमानित पाठ पर मन्या, कृकाटिका, विधुर, फण, अपाङ्ग और आवर्त: चवालीस जो वैकल्य यानी अपूर्णता करने वाले हैं, सौम्य होने से।
english: Kūrca, jānu, kūrpara, āṇi, urvī, lohitākhya, viṭapa, kakṣādhara, kukundara, aṃsaphalaka, nīlā, manyā (on a conjectural reading), kṛkāṭikā, vidhura, phaṇa, apāṅga and āvarta: forty-four that cause impairment (vaikalya), because of their saumya (soft, of Soma) nature.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mandyā' is not a marma name; 'manyā' is the usual name between nīlā and kṛkāṭikā (see 58, where 'manmā' is printed); n-d for n-y is a plausible OCR error

notes: Printed 'kūrcca' (double c) is normalised to kūrca (orthographic, as in 59); recorded once, no flag. The long run-together token is split by name and the join of 'catuścatvāriṃśad-vaikalya-' follows the print. 'vaikalya' = impairment, defect of a limb or organ; the exact modern equivalent (deformity, disability) is not stated. The count 'forty-four' is as printed. The emended manyā is conjectural and marked so in both translations. 'kūrparāṇyurvī' is read as kūrpara + āṇi + urvī (āṇi is the marma of u11). COUNT CHECK (observation): the printed names then give 42 (kūrca 4, jānu 2, kūrpara 2, āṇi 4, urvī 4, lohitākhya 4, viṭapa 2, kakṣādhara 2, kukundara 2, aṃsaphalaka 2, nīlā 2, manyā 2, kṛkāṭikā 2, vidhura 2, phaṇa 2, apāṅga 2, āvarta 2); the printed forty-four needs aṃsa (2) as well, which may be hidden in 'kukuṃdarāṃsaphalaka' (a lost repeated aṃsa); left as printed, open.

hindi: क्योंकि सोम स्थिरता और शीतलता से प्राणों को धारण करता है। और वे भी कभी आहत होने पर मार देते हैं।
english: For Soma sustains the life-breaths (prāṇa) by steadiness and coolness. And those too, when struck, sometimes kill.
notes: [02.07.68] 'Soma' = the moon-principle, cool and steady. 'dhārayati' is a causative form with the plain sense 'holds, sustains'. [02.07.69] 'tāni' refers to the saumya marmas of 67. The object (the person) is not printed.

hindi: कूर्चशिरस्, गुल्फ यानी टखना और मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई: आठ पीड़ा के स्रोत, अग्नि, वायु और सोम के गुणों की अधिकता से।
english: Kūrcaśiras, gulpha (ankle) and maṇibandha (wrist), however: eight sources of pain (ruj), because of an abundance of the qualities of Agni, Vāyu and Soma.
notes: Printed 'kūrcca' normalised to kūrca (see 67). The count 'eight' is as printed. 'ākara' = mine, source. Verbless; no verb supplied.

hindi: क्योंकि अग्नि और वायु विशेष रूप से पीड़ा के स्रोत।
english: For Agni and Vāyu, especially, the two sources of pain.
notes: Verbless; no verb supplied. Explains 70.

hindi: किन्तु सोम अनुमानित पाठ पर प्राणों को सहारा देता है, ऐसा कहा गया है।
english: But Soma upholds the life-breaths (on a conjectural reading); thus it has been said.

text_flags.why: possible: 'valaṃbata' is not a form; the verb avalambate (supports) with a lost initial a (and -ta for -te) fits 68 (Soma sustains the life-breaths), and 'ha' for 'i' in 'ityuktaṃ' is a plausible OCR error

notes: The reading is conjectural: 'valaṃbata' emended to avalambate and 'hatyuktam' to 'ityuktam'; the sense (Soma supports life) agrees with 68. The sandhi 'prāṇān avalambata' would normally give 'prāṇānavalambata'; the print drops the a-, which supports the damage. The unit closes the marma-classification passage.

hindi: दूसरे तो कहते हैं।
english: Others, however, say.
notes: GROUPING: appears to introduce the statements of the 'others' in the following units (74 onward). 'āhuḥ' is a perfect form with present sense.

words.gloss: without the dart (viśalya); killing (ghna); viśalyaghna = killing when the dart is removed (standard sense)

hindi: विशल्यघ्न यानी शल्य निकाले जाने पर मारने वाले, मांस आदि पाँचों के भी अत्यन्त बढ़े हुओं के मेल से।
english: Viśalyaghna (ones, those that kill when the dart is removed), through the coming together of even the five, flesh and the rest, greatly increased.

text_flags.why: possible: the genitive plural of pañcan is pañcānām; the long ā of the ending appears to be lost in print

notes: Elliptical: no verb; the neuter plural 'viśalyaghnāni' stands for an unstated noun and is shown as '(ones)'. The five are not named in this unit ('māṃsa-ādi' = flesh and the rest). 'viśalyaghna' = 'killing when the dart (śalya) is removed' is the usual sense of the term; this unit does not spell it out. 'vivṛddha' (greatly increased) may qualify the five or be read with 'samavāya'. GROUPING: appears to be the first statement of the 'others' introduced in 73, and continues in 75-76.

words.gram: m. abl. sg. used as adverb

hindi: एक-एक से घटे हुओं और अल्पों के क्रम से अन्य; और दूसरे लोग स्वभाव से ही कहते हैं।
english: Of those reduced by one each, and of the small ones, in order, the other (ones); and others say, by nature alone.
notes: Elliptical: no verb for the first clause; the things reduced by one each are not named (they appear to be the five of 74, but the unit does not say so). 'itarāṇi' (other ones) stands for an unstated noun. The join is uncertain: 'svabhāvataḥ eva' may instead go with 'itarāṇi' ('the others by nature alone'), leaving 'ca anye vadanti' as 'and others say'. Regular sandhi: svabhāvataḥ + eva = svabhāvata eva. GROUPING: appears to continue 74.

words.gloss: moon; sun; ayaskānta (lodestone; standard); stones (candra and sūrya stones: probably moonstone and sunstone, probable)

hindi: प्रत्येक के अपने नियत कर्म वाले, चन्द्र और सूर्य पत्थरों यानी सम्भवतः चन्द्रकान्त और सूर्यकान्त, तथा अयस्कान्त यानी चुम्बक पत्थर के जल, अग्नि और लोहे से मिलन की भाँति; और वैसे ही बहुत मर्मों वाले हाथ-पैर कट जाने पर भी स्वभाव से ही मृत्यु नहीं।
english: With each its own fixed function, like the unions of the candra and sūrya stones (probably moonstone and sunstone) and the ayaskānta (lodestone) with water, fire and iron; and likewise, when the hands and feet, though having many marmas, are cut off, by nature itself no death.

text_flags.why: possible: the lodestone is ayaskānta with long ā (the long ā is lost in print); also 'vanhi' is the older spelling of vahni, normalised in `w`

notes: Identifications: ayaskānta = lodestone (standard); candra and sūrya stones = moonstone and sunstone (probable; the pairing of the three stones with water, fire and iron in order is natural but not stated). 'vanhi' is the printed spelling of vahni (orthographic, normalised in 'w'). 'pratiniyata-karman' = each having its own fixed action. 'chinneṣu ... pāṇipādeṣu' is a locative absolute; no verb is supplied for 'na mṛtyuḥ'. GROUPING: appears to continue 74-75 (the view of those who say 'by nature'). REVIEW: traditionally candrakānta (moon-crystal) is said to exude water in moonlight and sūryakānta (sun-crystal) to yield fire in sunlight; modern moonstone/sunstone are different minerals, so the identification stays hedged (probable, identity disputed).
lines_deva: प्रतिनियतकर्माणि चंद्रसूर्यायस्कंतोपलानामिवांबुवन्हिलोहसंश्लेषाः तथा च छिन्नेषु बहुमर्मस्वपि पाणिपादेषु स्वभावत एव न मृत्युः
lines_iast: pratiniyatakarmāṇi caṃdrasūryāyaskaṃtopalānāmivāṃbuvanhilohasaṃśleṣāḥ tathā ca chinneṣu bahumarmasvapi pāṇipādeṣu svabhāvata eva na mṛtyuḥ

hindi: दूसरे फिर यहाँ भी कारण बताते हैं।
english: Others again state a reason here also.
notes: GROUPING: appears to introduce the reason given in 78.

hindi: क्योंकि हाथ-पैर के कटने पर सिराएँ यानी सम्भवतः शिराएँ सिकुड़ जाती हैं; इसलिए रक्त के थोड़े बहने से जीवन; पर मर्म के बिंधने पर रक्त के अत्यधिक बहने से और वायु की विकृति से मृत्यु।
english: For, on the cutting off of hands and feet, the sirā (vessels, probably veins) contract; hence, from slight flow of blood, life; but, on the piercing of a marma, from excessive flow of blood and from abnormality of wind (vāyu), death.

text_flags.why: possible: the compound is alpa-asṛj-prasruti; 'asrak' looks like a print slip with ṛ lost as ra
possible: the ablative in -tas (atirakta-srutitaḥ) parallels alpāsṛk-prasruteḥ in the first half; the anusvara before -to looks like a stray sign

notes: Elliptical: 'jīvitam' (life) and 'maraṇam' (death) have no verb; none is supplied. sirā = vessel or channel; 'veins' is a probable modern equivalent only (the word is used for vessels in general). 'vāyu' = wind; whether the doṣa Vāta is meant is not stated. The two corrections in `text_flags` are used in `words` but the translation does not depend on them beyond the sense 'from flow of blood'. GROUPING: appears to complete the reason announced in 77.
lines_deva: पाणिपादच्छेदे हि सिराः संकोचमायांति ततोऽल्पास्रक्प्रस्रुतेर्जीवितं मर्मव्यधे त्वतिरक्तस्रुतिंतो वायुवैकृतेन च मरणं
lines_iast: pāṇipādacchede hi sirāḥ saṃkocamāyāṃti tato'lpāsrakprasruterjīvitaṃ marmavyadhe tvatiraktasrutiṃto vāyuvaikṛtena ca maraṇaṃ

hindi: इसलिए मर्म पर चोट खाए हुए का वह अंग शीघ्र सन्धि के स्थान पर काट देना चाहिए।
english: Therefore, of one struck on a marma, that limb should be cut off quickly at the place of a joint (sandhi).
notes: 'sandhideśāt' (ablative) is rendered 'at the place of a joint'. sandhi = joint (standard). 'tadaṅgam' = that limb, i.e. the one struck. GROUPING: appears to follow 78 as its conclusion.

words.gloss: slightly, a little; at the end (sense unclear here)

hindi: अत्यन्त चोट खाए मर्मों का अपने-अपने अनुसार कर्म: पूर्व-पूर्व वाला; या ईषत् अन्ते यानी थोड़ा, अन्त में; यह अंश अस्पष्ट है, चोट खाए हुओं का केवल बाद वाला।
english: But of marmas that are severely struck, each according to its own, the action: each preceding one; or, 'īṣat ante' (slightly, at the end; this part unclear), of those struck, only the latter.
notes: Obscure; no verb. Plain reading offered: for severely struck marmas the action is that of each preceding (item); for the others struck, only the latter. What the preceding and the latter items are is not stated in this unit. 'īṣadaṃte' is not clear: it may be īṣat + ante, or a damaged form; it is left unclear in both translations. 'pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ' is a distributive repetition ('each preceding'). GROUPING: appears to continue 79 (what follows a blow on a marma).
lines_deva: अतिहतानां तु मर्मणां यथास्वं पूर्वं पूर्वं च कर्म ईषदंते वा हतानामुत्तरमेव
lines_iast: atihatānāṃ tu marmaṇāṃ yathāsvaṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca karma īṣadaṃte vā hatānāmuttarameva

hindi: और फिर पाँच प्रकार से विभाजित किया जाता है।
english: And again, (it) is divided fivefold.
notes: The subject is not stated (the marmas, from the chapter's subject). GROUPING: appears to introduce the fivefold division that 82 and the following units (83-87, five groups by measure) set out.

hindi: वह इस प्रकार:
english: Namely:
notes: Introductory formula (tad yathā). GROUPING: appears to introduce the list in 83-87.

hindi: ऊर्वी, कूर्चशिरस्, दो विटप और दो कक्षाधर: बारह, अपने अंगुल के माप के।
english: Ūrvī (plural), kūrcaśiras (plural), the two viṭapa and the two kakṣādhara: twelve, measured by one's own finger-breadth (aṅgula).
notes: These are names of marmas, the subject of the chapter; the unit itself does not say 'marma' and has no verb. 'viṭape' and 'kakṣādhare' are read as duals (probable; they could also be locatives). The numbers within the twelve are not given; the plurals ūrvyaḥ and kūrcaśirāṃsi plus the two duals fit the total only if the plurals are four each, which the text does not state. 'svāṅgula' = the person's own finger-breadth; the Sanskrit gives no number before it.
lines_deva: ऊर्व्यः कूर्चशिरांसि विटपे कक्षाधरे च द्वादश स्वांगुलोन्मितानि
lines_iast: ūrvyaḥ kūrcaśirāṃsi viṭape kakṣādhare ca dvādaśa svāṃgulonmitāni

hindi: दो गुल्फ यानी टखने, दो मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई और दो स्तनमूल यानी स्तन का आधार: छह, दो अंगुल के। दो जानु यानी घुटने और दो कूर्पर यानी कोहनी: चार, तीन अंगुल के।
english: The two gulpha (ankle), the two maṇibandha (wrist) and the two stanamūla (base of the breast): six, of two finger-breadths (aṅgula). The two jānu (knee) and the two kūrpara (elbow): four, of three finger-breadths (aṅgula).
notes: [02.07.84] Names of marmas that are also names of body parts; the unit names only the parts. No verb. 'caṣaṭ' is printed run together (ca ṣaṭ, spacing slip). 'stanamūle' is read as a dual; it could also be a locative singular. [02.07.85] Names of marmas that are also names of body parts; no verb. The duals are read from the endings (-ī, -e).

words.gloss: manyā (name; the word also means nape of the neck)

hindi: कूर्च, गुद यानी मलद्वार, बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय, नाभि, हृदय, दो नीला, दो मन्या, मातृकाएँ, सीमन्त और शृंगाटक: उनतीस, हथेली के माप के।
english: The kūrca (plural), guda (anus), basti (bladder), nābhi (navel), hṛdaya (heart), the two nīlā, the two manyā, the mātṛkā (plural), the sīmanta (plural) and the śṛṅgāṭaka (plural): twenty-nine, measured by the palm (pāṇitala).
notes: Names of marmas; several are also body-part names. No verb. 'kūrcā gudo' is regular sandhi (kūrcāḥ gudaḥ). 'nīle manye' are read as duals. The numbers within the twenty-nine are not given in the text. 'basti' here = bladder (the body part), not the enema bag or enema. 'sīmanta' and 'śṛṅgāṭaka' are kept as names; the literal meanings in the glosses are the ordinary senses of the words, not a claim about the structure.
lines_deva: कूर्चा गुदोबस्तिर्नाभिर्हृदयं नीले मन्ये मातृकाः सीमंताः शृंगाटकानि चैकोनत्रिंशत्पाणितलसंमितानि
lines_iast: kūrcā gudobastirnābhirhṛdayaṃ nīle manye mātṛkāḥ sīmaṃtāḥ śṛṃgāṭakāni caikonatriṃśatpāṇitalasaṃmitāni

words.gloss: finger-breadth (aṅgula); dala (half, probable; literally 'petal, part'); measure

hindi: शेष छप्पन, अंगुलदल के माप के यानी सम्भवतः आधे अंगुल के।
english: The remaining: fifty-six, of the measure of an aṅgula-dala (probably half a finger-breadth).
notes: No verb. 'dala' = half is probable (the word also means petal or part). The printed numbers in 83-87 are 12, 6, 4, 29 and 56, which add up to 107; the text does not state this total here.

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others again say.
notes: GROUPING: appears to introduce the views of other authorities on the measures, in 89-91.

words.gloss: rice grain (vrīhi; Oryza sativa, standard); measure

hindi: व्रीहि यानी धान के दाने के माप के: क्षिप्र।
english: Of the measure of a vrīhi (rice grain): the kṣipra.
notes: No verb. 'kṣiprāṇi' is read as the marma name kṣipra (neuter plural); the alternative is the plain adjective 'quick'. GROUPING: appears to follow 88 and continues in 90-91.

words.gloss: sesame seed (tila; Sesamum indicum, standard); measure

hindi: कलाय यानी सम्भवतः मटर के माप के: स्तनरोहित और उत्क्षेप। वैसे ही दूसरे लोग तिल के माप के भी मर्म मानते हैं।
english: Of the measure of a kalāya (probably the pea): the stanarohita and the utkṣepa. Likewise others accept marmas even of the measure of a tila (sesame seed).
notes: [02.07.90] No verb. kalāya = pea, probable (another pulse, grass pea, is a possible alternative). 'stanarohita' and 'utkṣepa' are marma names, read as two names in a dvandva. GROUPING: appears to continue 89. [02.07.91] 'icchanti' literally 'they wish for'; 'accept' is the natural sense here. The avagraha printed after -ā (tathā'nye) is a print habit. GROUPING: appears to continue 88-90.

hindi: और यहाँ हैं:
english: And here there are:
notes: Formula introducing the verses that follow; the noun (verses) is not stated. GROUPING: appears to introduce 93 onward.

hindi: मर्मव्यामे भी, यह शब्द अस्पष्ट है, इस शरीर में आयु मर्मों की रक्षा करती है। इसलिए विचक्षण को सदा आयु में व्याप्त रहने वाले का ही सेवन करना चाहिए।
english: Even in marmavyāme (unclear), in this body, life guards the marmas. Therefore the discerning (man) should always attend only to what pervades life (āyur-vyāpi).

text_flags.why: possible: pta/ma is a known OCR confusion in this print and 'marma-vyāpta' (pervaded by marmas) would fit 'dehe'; but 'vyāma' (span, fathom) gives no clear sense; no reading is adopted

notes: [02.07.93] 'marmavyāme' is left unsplit and unclear; the conjecture in the flag is not used in the translations. 'āyuḥ' and 'marmāṇi' are both nominative/accusative-looking neuters; with the singular verb 'rakṣati' the singular 'āyuḥ' is taken as subject (so 'life guards the marmas'), but 'marmāṇi' as subject with 'āyuḥ' as object, or 'āyur-marmāṇi' as a compound, cannot be excluded. Regular sandhi: dehe asminn āyur. Metre: 16 syllables as printed. GROUPING: appears to open the verses announced in 92. [02.07.94] Obscure. 'āyurvyāpi' is read as 'life-pervading' (n.), standing for an unstated object; the case is uncertain and the object of 'seveta' is not named. 'sev' can also mean serve, practise or enjoy. GROUPING: appears to continue 93 ('tasmāt'). Metre: 16 syllables as printed.

hindi: मर्म पर थोड़ी भी चोट प्रायः बहुत अधिक पीड़ित करती है। मर्म में आश्रय वाले रोग वैसे ही, प्रयत्न से भी आरम्भ किए हुए।
english: A blow on a marma, even a slight one, generally afflicts exceedingly. Diseases that have a marma as their seat are likewise, set about (prakrāntāḥ) even with effort.
notes: [02.07.95] The object of 'bādhate' (afflicts) is not stated. 'svalpaḥ api prāyaśaḥ' is printed run together (svalpo'piprāyaśo), a spacing slip. 'tarām' = exceedingly or more. [02.07.96] Obscure; no predicate is stated here (the verb 'bādhate' of 95 may be carried, but the unit does not say so). 'prakrānta' = begun, set about; whether it means 'treatment undertaken' or 'set in' is not clear and is not enriched. Regular sandhi: rogāḥ marma- (rogā marmā-). GROUPING: appears to continue 95 and to lead into the signs given in 97-99.

hindi: वह बहुत इधर-उधर फेंका जाता है, डूबता हुआ, शून्य, घूमता है, काँपता है। वह कठिनाई से ऊपर की ओर साँस लेता है, ढीले अंगों वाला, बार-बार।
